# Indikator 7b

## Synthesis

Indikator 7b is a quality indicator used in Denmark's ADHD-databasen (ADHD database) to measure the share of young people in the so-called "ADHD-behandlingspopulation" (ADHD treatment population) who have passed the *folkeskolens afgangseksamen* — the Danish primary and lower secondary school leaving examination — before turning 17 [^src1]. It is one of several indicators tracked to assess outcomes for people diagnosed with and treated for ADHD in the Danish healthcare system, and it appears in the ADHD database's annual report covering the period 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025 [^src1].

According to the report, fulfilment of Indikator 7b was 58% (with a confidence interval of 55–60%) for the period 01.04.2024–31.03.2025 [^src1]. This represents a decline from prior years: fulfilment stood at 66% for the 2023/24 period and 67% for 2022/23 [^src1]. The downward trend places Indikator 7b among the indicators discussed in the broader report, which found that most of the ADHD database's quality indicators fall well short of the development goal of ≥90% fulfilment, underscoring ongoing concerns about the quality of ADHD diagnosis and treatment across the Danish healthcare system. The report itself describes work underway to revise and refine the indicator set — including new indicators for adult ADHD patients — so that it better reflects clinical practice.

No relationships involving Indikator 7b are documented in the available source material.
